electron_flow.name: External Circuit (Electron Flow)
acceptable: Electron flow from anode to cathode
electron_flow.description: Metallic conductor carrying electrons through the external circuit from the oxidised anode (Zn) to the cathode (Cu).

salt_bridge.name: Salt Bridge
salt_bridge.description: Inverted U-tube filled with a saturated inert electrolyte (such as KCl or KNO₃) that completes the circuit and maintains electrical neutrality in both half-cells by ion migration.

anode_electrode.name: Zinc Anode (Negative Electrode)
anode_electrode.description: Negative electrode where oxidation occurs (Zn(s) → Zn²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻), causing the metal strip to decrease in mass over time.

anode_electrolyte.name: Zinc Sulfate Electrolyte (ZnSO₄(aq))
anode_electrolyte.description: Aqueous half-cell solution (1 mol·dm⁻³ at standard conditions) containing Zn²⁺ ions into which oxidised cations dissolve.

voltmeter.name: High-Resistance Voltmeter
voltmeter.description: High-resistance instrument connected across the two electrodes to measure the potential difference (emf / E°cell) between the half-cells.

cathode_electrode.name: Copper Cathode (Positive Electrode)
cathode_electrode.description: Positive electrode where reduction occurs (Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Cu(s)), causing solid copper to plate onto the electrode and increase its mass.

porous_plug.name: Porous Cotton Wool Plug
porous_plug.description: Permeable barrier at the ends of the salt bridge that allows mobile ions to migrate while preventing bulk mixing of the half-cell electrolytes.

cathode_electrolyte.name: Copper(II) Sulfate Electrolyte (CuSO₄(aq))
cathode_electrolyte.description: Blue aqueous half-cell solution containing Cu²⁺ ions that are reduced and deposited onto the cathode surface.
